application.name: get_recent_files
application.description: Get the files recently opened in Spyder (shown in File > Open recent), most recent first.

debugger.name: debug_command
debugger.description:
Run a debugger (Pdb) command in an IPython console that is debugging, and get its output and the new location. For instance: `n` (next line), `s` (step into), `r` (return), `c` (continue), `u`/`d` (move up/down the stack), `w` (where), `l` (list code), `a` (arguments), `b file:line` (breakpoint), `p expr` or `pp expr` (evaluate an expression in the current frame) or `q` (stop debugging).

If another agent's code is being debugged in the console, only that agent can send commands.

console_id.description: Id of the console, as returned by list_consoles. By default, the console currently selected in Spyder.

timeout.description: Seconds to wait for the command to finish (e.g. `c` runs until the next breakpoint) before returning the output collected so far.

debugger.name: get_debug_state
debugger.description: Get whether an IPython console is debugging and, if so, the current location and the call stack (oldest frame first), with the index of the frame the debugger is in.

console_id.description: Id of the console, as returned by list_consoles. By default, the console currently selected in Spyder.

debugger.name: list_breakpoints
debugger.description: List the breakpoints set in Spyder, with their file, line and condition.

debugger.name: set_breakpoint
debugger.description: Set a breakpoint, which stops code run with debugging (e.g. with start_debugging) when it reaches the line. It's shown in the Editor.

line.description: Line number (1-based). It can't be blank or a comment.

condition.description: Python expression; the debugger only stops if it's true.

debugger.name: start_debugging
debugger.description: Start debugging a Python file in an IPython console, like pressing Ctrl+F5 in Spyder. The debugger stops at the first breakpoint of the file if it has any (see set_breakpoint) or else at its first line. Then use debug_command to step through the code and inspect it.

filename.description: Absolute path of the file. If it's open in the Editor, its current contents are debugged, including unsaved changes.

args.description: Command line arguments for the file.

console_id.description: Id of the console, as returned by list_consoles. By default, the console currently selected in Spyder.

timeout.description: Seconds to wait for the console to be free and the debugger to stop before returning the output collected so far.

editor.name: edit_file
editor.description: Replace text in a file through Spyder's Editor, which opens the file if needed. Unlike writing the file on disk, the change is applied to what the user sees, including their unsaved changes, and they can undo it with Ctrl+Z. The file isn't saved: use save_file for that.

old_text.description: Text to replace. It must match the Editor's contents exactly, including indentation (see read_editor_file), and appear only once unless replace_all is true.

editor.name: get_diagnostics
editor.description: Get the errors and warnings that Spyder's code analysis (pyflakes, pycodestyle, etc.) shows for a file open in the Editor, with their line and column (1-based). They're updated a moment after the file changes, and are only available if code completion and linting are enabled in Spyder.

filename.description: Absolute path of the file. By default, the current file.

editor.name: get_editor_state
editor.description: Get the file the user is looking at in Spyder's Editor, the cursor position (1-based), the selected text and the list of open files, including which ones have unsaved changes. Use it to find out what the user refers to with "this file", "this function" or "the selection".

editor.name: new_editor_file
editor.description: Create a new, unsaved file in Spyder's Editor with the given contents, e.g. to show the user code to review. Returns its name.

editor.name: open_file
editor.description: Open a file in Spyder's Editor to show it to the user, optionally at a given line.

editor.name: read_editor_file
editor.description: Read the contents of a file open in Spyder's Editor, including unsaved changes that are not on disk yet.

filename.description: Absolute path of the file. By default, the current file.

editor.name: save_file
editor.description: Save a file open in Spyder's Editor to disk, e.g. after edit_file. It also saves any other unsaved changes the user made in that file.

explorer.name: get_files_folder
explorer.description: Get the folder the user is browsing in the Files pane.

ipython_console.name: execute_code
ipython_console.description:
Run Python code in one of Spyder's IPython consoles and get its output (stdout, stderr, results and tracebacks) and the figures it displays, as images.

The code runs in the user's live kernel, so variables persist between calls, and the user sees the code and its output in the console. IPython magics are supported. Figures also appear in Spyder's Plots pane.

If the console is busy (e.g. the user or another agent is running code in it), the code waits for it to be free. The user goes first: the code doesn't start while they're typing in the console.

console_id.description: Id of the console to use, as returned by list_consoles. By default, the console currently selected in Spyder.

timeout.description: Seconds to wait for the console to be free and the code to finish before returning the output collected so far. The code keeps running, but it doesn't run if the console is still busy.

ipython_console.name: get_console_history
ipython_console.description: Get the last inputs run in an IPython console since its kernel started (by the user or with execute_code), oldest first. Use it to see what the user did, e.g. to turn it into a script.

console_id.description: Id of the console, as returned by list_consoles. By default, the console currently selected in Spyder.

ipython_console.name: get_object_help
ipython_console.description: Get the signature, docstring, module and package version of a function, class or module, as installed in the environment of an IPython console. Objects don't need to be imported in the console (e.g. `pandas.DataFrame.merge`).

name.description: Name of the object, e.g. `np.linspace` or `pandas.DataFrame.merge`.

console_id.description: Id of the console, as returned by list_consoles. By default, the console currently selected in Spyder.

ipython_console.name: inspect_variable
ipython_console.description: Get a summary of a variable in an IPython console without running code in it: the type and, depending on it, the shape, dtypes, missing values, first rows and statistics (DataFrames and Series), the shape, dtype and range (arrays), the length and a preview (collections) or the repr (other objects).

name.description: Name of the variable, or an attribute of it (e.g. `df` or `model.coef_`).

console_id.description: Id of the console, as returned by list_consoles. By default, the console currently selected in Spyder.

ipython_console.name: interrupt_console
ipython_console.description: Interrupt the code you're running in an IPython console, like pressing Ctrl+C, and cancel your code that is waiting for the console. Code run by the user or other agents can't be interrupted.

console_id.description: Id of the console, as returned by list_consoles. By default, the console currently selected in Spyder.

ipython_console.name: list_consoles
ipython_console.description: List the IPython consoles open in Spyder, with their id, name, state (idle, busy, debugging or starting), working directory (where relative paths in code run there are resolved), which one is the current console, who is running code in it (`user`, `you` or the name of another agent), how many runs are waiting for it, and who created it if an agent did (with new_console).

ipython_console.name: list_variables
ipython_console.description: List the variables defined in an IPython console, with their type, size and a short preview of their value, as shown in Spyder's Variable Explorer. Use execute_code to inspect a variable in more detail.

console_id.description: Id of the console, as returned by list_consoles. By default, the console currently selected in Spyder.

ipython_console.name: new_console
ipython_console.description: Open a new IPython console with its own kernel, e.g. to run long or risky computations without blocking or changing the user's console. It doesn't share variables with other consoles. The console the user has selected doesn't change, so pass the returned id as console_id to the other tools to use it.

name.description: Name for the console's tab, e.g. the agent's name.

wdir.description: Working directory of the new console. By default, the one Spyder uses for new consoles.

ipython_console.name: run_cell
ipython_console.description: Run a cell (a block delimited by `# %%` comments) of a file open in the Editor in an IPython console, like pressing Shift+Enter in Spyder, and get its output. The cell's current contents in the Editor run, including unsaved changes.

filename.description: Absolute path of the file. It's opened in the Editor if needed.

cell.description: Index of the cell (0-based, the code before the first `# %%` is cell 0 if there's any) or its name (the text after `# %%`).

console_id.description: Id of the console, as returned by list_consoles. By default, the console currently selected in Spyder.

timeout.description: Seconds to wait for the console to be free and the cell to finish before returning the output collected so far. It keeps running.

ipython_console.name: run_file
ipython_console.description: Run a Python file in an IPython console, like pressing F5 in Spyder, and get its output. If the file is open in the Editor, its current contents run, including unsaved changes.

args.description: Command line arguments for the file.

wdir.description: Working directory to run the file in. By default, the file's directory.

console_id.description: Id of the console, as returned by list_consoles. By default, the console currently selected in Spyder.

timeout.description: Seconds to wait for the console to be free and the file to finish before returning the output collected so far. It keeps running.

mcp_server.name: list_agent_sessions
mcp_server.description: List the AI agent sessions connected to Spyder, including yours, with their name and whether they're running a Spyder tool now. Use it to coordinate with them, e.g. before restarting a console or opening a project, which affect everyone. list_consoles shows which consoles each one runs code in.

plots.name: get_figure
plots.description: Get a figure from Spyder's Plots pane as an image, to look at plots generated in a console.

index.description: Index of the figure, as given by list_figures. Negative values count from the end, so -1 is the most recent figure.

console_id.description: Id of the console, as returned by list_consoles. By default, the console currently selected in Spyder.

plots.name: list_figures
plots.description: List the figures shown in Spyder's Plots pane for a console, oldest first, with their index, format and size in pixels.

console_id.description: Id of the console, as returned by list_consoles. By default, the console currently selected in Spyder.

profiler.name: get_profile_results
profiler.description: Get the results of the last profiling in an IPython console (by the user or with profile_code or profile_file): the functions where it spent the most time or, for one function, the functions that called it and the ones it called, with the time spent through each.

console_id.description: Id of the console, as returned by list_consoles. By default, the console currently selected in Spyder.

function.description: Function to get the callers and callees of, by name (e.g. `solve`) or location (e.g. `model.py:42`).

sort.description: Sort functions by `local` time (spent in the function itself), `total` time (including the functions it called) or number of `calls`.

include_libraries.description: Whether to include functions from libraries, the standard library and built-ins, or only the user's code.

profiler.name: profile_code
profiler.description:
Profile Python code in an IPython console and get its output and the functions where it spent the most time, measured with cProfile. The results are also shown in Spyder's Profiler pane. Use get_profile_results to see the callers and callees of a function.

The code runs like with execute_code: in the user's live kernel, waiting for the console to be free, and slower than usual because of the profiling.

console_id.description: Id of the console, as returned by list_consoles. By default, the console currently selected in Spyder.

timeout.description: Seconds to wait for the console to be free and the code to finish. If it doesn't finish in time, use get_profile_results once it does.

limit.description: Maximum number of functions in the results.

profiler.name: profile_file
profiler.description: Profile a Python file in an IPython console, like Run > Profile in Spyder, and get its output and the functions where it spent the most time. If the file is open in the Editor, its current contents run, including unsaved changes.

args.description: Command line arguments for the file.

wdir.description: Working directory to run the file in. By default, the file's directory.

console_id.description: Id of the console, as returned by list_consoles. By default, the console currently selected in Spyder.

timeout.description: Seconds to wait for the console to be free and the file to finish. If it doesn't finish in time, use get_profile_results once it does.

limit.description: Maximum number of functions in the results.

project_explorer.name: close_project
project_explorer.description: Close the project open in Spyder, after the user confirms it. The agent sessions of the project (not yours) are closed too.

project_explorer.name: get_active_project
project_explorer.description: Get the root directory of the project open in Spyder, or null if there's none.

project_explorer.name: open_project
project_explorer.description:
Open a folder as the project in Spyder, after the user confirms it. If it isn't a Spyder project yet, it becomes one.

Opening a project restarts all of Spyder's IPython consoles (yours too), so the variables, imports and figures in them are lost, and closes the agent sessions of the project that was open (not yours). Ask the user before if it's not clear they want it.

workingdir.name: get_workdir
workingdir.description: Get Spyder's current working directory, which the IPython consoles and the Files pane use by default.
